name: Ledger — Shelf Mutual Credit & Trust Net
subcategory: grassroots reputation and mutual credit network
description: Ledger is the Shelf's answer to corporate reputation systems like Meridian Score and Stratum — a community-run mutual credit and trust network that operates entirely on peer attestation rather than algorithmic scoring. Built in 2191 by a collective of Tier 1 market organizers in the Ward 7 Ghost Market district, Ledger tracks not creditworthiness in the corporate sense but community trustworthiness: did you show up, did you pay your debts, did you look out for your neighbors, did you snitch. Reputation on Ledger is expressed in 'marks' — positive and negative attestations left by named community members — and a high Ledger standing can open doors to ghost market stalls, housing collectives, and mutual aid networks that no amount of Quanta can buy. The platform runs on a patchwork of donated hardware and volunteer coders and has never taken a corporate credit.
cultural_impact: Ledger has become the de facto trust infrastructure for Tier 1 community economics, enabling ghost markets, housing collectives, and informal lending circles to function without corporate financial systems. Its reputation model — community-attested, name-linked, and transparent — is studied by sociologists as a working alternative to algorithmic social credit.
key_figures: Blessing Tran-Okonkwo (founding organizer, Ward 7 Ghost Market)
Ikenna Sorensen-Mwangi (current platform steward and lead coder)
The Ledger Council (seven rotating community representatives who arbitrate disputes)
story_hooks: A corporate intelligence contractor has been systematically mapping Ledger's social graph to identify Shelf community leaders for preemptive disruption before a planned Shelf rezoning — and someone just found the contractor's scraper bot in the network logs.

A high-Ledger-standing community elder is accused of a serious betrayal by a single anonymous mark — but Ledger requires named attestations, meaning someone created a false identity to leave it, and the Ledger Council must decide how to respond without destroying the platform's integrity.

A Tier 3 sociologist publishes a paper arguing Ledger's reputation model is superior to Meridian Score for predicting prosocial behavior — and now a corponation wants to license the model, and the Ledger Council has to decide what 'no' means when the offer is Φ4 million.
user_base: Approximately 340,000 active users; almost exclusively Tier 1 Shelf residents, with small Tier 2 crossover among those with Shelf community ties
monetization: No monetization — sustained by donated hardware, volunteer labor, and small community levies from ghost market operators who use the platform
notable_feature: The 'Named Mark' requirement — all attestations, positive and negative, must be left under a user's real verified community identity, making reputation attacks costly and accountability genuine in a way no anonymous system can replicate
